To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the radar processing system developed in the Bollene-2 project is able to provide accurate rainfall estimates over the mountainous region of the Cévenne–Vivarais region.

1) the use of a volume-scanning radar strategy for rainfall estimation in the Cévenes–Vivarais region is feasible, 2) the use of the space–time-adaptation strategy for radar processing provides the best performance, 3) the use of an adaptive radar processing system is essential for improving radar rainfall estimation in mountainous terrain, and 4) the use of noncoherent radar data is not a limitation for radar rainfall estimations.
a radar rainfall estimation strategy for the Cévennais–Vivarais region of France has been developed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology for estimating precipitation in a mountainous environment using the C-band radar located in Bollène, France.
developing radar processing strategies and techniques that are appropriate to the complex terrain of the French Cevennes–Vivaraiis region.
the development of an efficient and accurate radar rainfall estimation technique that will be useful to the French National Water and Forest Agency for hydrological applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the space–time-adapted radar rainfall estimator has performed better in the mountainous terrain of the Cévennais–Vivarais region of France than the nonadapted and time-adapted radar algorithms.
the Bollene- 2002 experiment has been successful in that it has demonstrated a radar volume-scanned strategy to produce quantitative rainfall estimation for mountainous terrain.

the Bollene- 2002 experiment is an important contribution to the understanding and application of the radar rainfall problem, and that the TRADHAR system and its algorithms have demonstrated a significant potential for improving the quality of radar rainfall estimations over mountainous terrain, especially when combined with a space–time radar processing approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a radar processing system, Traitements Regionalizes et Adaptatifs des Donnees Radar pour Hydrologie (TRADAR), that is able to produce radar-based precipitation estimates in the mountainous region of Cevennes-Vivarais.
The main takeaway from our work is that

radar rainfall estimates can be improved in the Cévenes–Vivarais region by using a radar processing strategy that combines the use of reflectivity profiles with the use of reflectivities at the ground level.

the space–time adaptive radar processing (STARP) technique can be successfully applied in mountainous regions to produce rainfall estimates that are more accurate than those produced by nonadaptive techniques.
the use of a space–time-adapted radar rainfall estimation procedure can improve the accuracy of rainfall estimates over the mountainous regions in the south of France.
